default_in_repayment.text: ix.	According to the information and explanations given to us, the Company has not defaulted in repayment of dues to banks. The Company has not issued any debentures and has availed a Term Loan from a bank. Term loans were applied for the purpose for which the loans were obtained.  We did not come across any data to suggest that funds raised for short term purposes were used for long term purpose. There were no loans raised during the year by pledging of securities held in its subsidiaries, joint ventures or associate companies.

fraud.text: xi.	To the best of our knowledge and according to the information and explanations given to us and based on the audit procedure performed, we report that no cases of fraud by the Company or no material fraud on the Company by its officers or employees has been noticed or reported during the year. Consequently, the requirement to file a report under sub-section (12) of section 143 of the Companies Act 2013 did not arise. The register for whistle-blower complaints have been reviewed during the year.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: In Maharashtra prior to 2017, Octroi charge was levied for inward material but from 01.01.2017 Octroi was abolished and Local Body Tax (LBT) was levied. A stay for same dispute filed by the Taloja Manufacturing Association, of which TCP, HCL is a part, has already been granted by High court. The case will be combined with other similar case and will be taken up for hearing. Next date of hearing is awaited.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Malanjkhand Copper Project (MCP), a unit of Hindustan Copper Limited filed Case No. MJC 1 of 2016 before the Civil Court, Baihar challenging notice dated 18.01.2007 received from the Municipal Council, Malanjkhand demanding a sum of Rs.74.87 crore against Terminal Tax with 10 times penalty for the period 2000-2006. MCP has deposited Rs.19 crore (approximately) as per self-assessment and in compliance with Orders of the Courts in the account of Municipal Council, Malajkhand. Status as per Last Disclosure: Vide final judgment dated 28.07.2025, the Civil Court, Baihar rejected HCL/MCP’s appeal. On 07.05.2025, HCL filed an application before the Additional Secretary (FA), Ministry of Mines, Government of India, and subsequently vide letter dated 16.05.2025 to Deputy Secretary (FA), Ministry of Mines, Government of India, under the Administrative Mechanism for Resolution of CPSE’s Disputes (AMRCD) mechanism to get relief. The matter is pending under AMRCD.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Case. No. MJC 1 of 2016, Civil Court, Baihar Hindustan Copper Limited, Malanjkhand Copper Project Vs. Municipal Council, Malanjkhand
tax_litigation.status: On 16.10.2025, HCL has filed a Revision Application before the Court of Additional District Judge, Baihar, praying for setting aside the Demand Bill dated 03.01.2007 issued by the Municipal Council, Malanjkhand; and the final judgment dated 28.07.2025 passed by the Civil Court, Baihar in Case No. MJC 01/2016. The matter is pending under AMRCD for Amicable Resolution.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Malanjkhand Copper Project (MCP), a unit of Hindustan Copper Limited filed Special Leave Petition No. 14928 of 2014 before the Supreme Court of India challenging notice dated 31.10.2012 received from the Municipal Council, Malajkhand demanding a sum of Rs.188.68 crore against Terminal Tax with 10 times penalty for the period 2006-2012. Vide Order dated 17.02.2025 Special Leave Petition No. 14928 of 2014, the Supreme Court directed HCL to deposit 50% of Rs.188.68 crore within 8 weeks from 17.02.2025. The matter has been disposed of by the Supreme Court vide Order dated 17.02.2025. Subsequently, HCL/MCP filed a Miscellaneous Application No. 838 of 2025 in respect of Order dated 17.02.2025 passed by the Supreme Court in SLP (C) No. 14928 of 2014, praying for allowing HCL to deposit Rs. 5.3 crores, which is the difference of Terminal Tax calculated by the Municipal Council, i.e., Rs. 17,18,94,364/- and amount paid by HCL/MCP as per self-assessment, i.e., Rs. 11.88 crores. Vide Order dated 05.05.2025, the Supreme Court dismissed HCL/MCP's application On 07.05.2025, HCL filed an application before the Additional Secretary (FA), Ministry of Mines, Government of India, and subsequently vide letter dated 16.05.2025 to Deputy Secretary (FA), Ministry of Mines, Government of India, under the Administrative Mechanism for Resolution of CPSE's Disputes (AMRCD) mechanism to get relief. Status as per Last Disclosure: On 05.08.2025, Municipal Council Malanjkhand filed Contempt Petition (Civil) No. 628 of 2025 against Shri Nagesh Shenoy, ED & Unit Head, HCL/MCP for contempt of Order of the Hon’ble Supreme Court dated 17.02.2025 in SLP (C) No. 14928 of 2014. The hearing is 09.12.2025.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Contempt Petition (Civil) No. 628 of 2025, Supreme Court Municipal Council , Malanjkhand Vs. Nagesh Shenoy
tax_litigation.status: HCL has filed reply in the matter during last hearing on 07.10.2025. The next date is fixed for 07.04.2026.

The Department has considered request of HCL and vide its Letter dated 19.05.2026 (received on 27.05.2026), has conveyed that on the basis of the data provided by the Company and the departmental water rates issued from time to time, the total outstanding amount from the year 2005 to October, 2025 has been estimated at Rs.87.926 crore. The total outstanding amount from the year 2000-01 to 2005 was Rs.4.247 crore, adding which the total outstanding amount till date has been estimated at Rs.92.166 crore (Water charges Rs.46.623 crore and Penalty of Rs.45.543 crore). The estimated outstanding water tax bill has been provided to Hindustan Copper Ltd for confirmation. The Company is evaluating the calculation made by the Water Resource Department Ghatshila, Jharkhand.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: 1) State Of Jharkhand 2) Secretary, Deptt Of Water Resources (Earlier Known As Irrigation Deptt) 3) Superintending Engineer, Baraj Circle, Subarnrekha Project, Deptt Of Water Resources 4) Executive Engineer, Subarnrekha Canal Division, Deptt Of Water Resources
tax_litigation.status: HCL has challenged the demand notice of water resource dept. over consumption of natural river stream water from river Subranrekha at Jharkhand High court. Discuss with Water Resource Department regarding out of court settlement due to non-notification by state government. Case is pending at the admission stage, next date of hearing is 01.09.2026.

penalties.details: Email dated 25.08.2026 received from BSE and Letter No. NSE/LIST-SOP/COMB/FINES/0954 dated 25.08.2026 received from NSE vide which both the Exchanges have imposed fine of Rs.14,43,140/- each for non-compliance of provisions of SEBI Listing Regulations pertaining to composition of the Board and Constitution of Committees for the quarter ended 30.06.2026. Company requested administrative Ministry to appoint the vacant posts of directors on the Board of HCL
penalties.impact: Rs.14,43,140/- each. HCL, being a Government Company, the power of appointment of directors on its Board as per its Articles of Association is vested with President of India, acting through the Ministry of Mines, Government of India. The Company has written to the Ministry of Mines, Government of India for appointment of required number of directors on the Board of HCL and the matter is under consideration. Consequent upon appointment of required number of directors on the Board of HCL, the Company will seek waiver of fines from both BSE and NSE. Hence, there is no impact on financial, operation or other activities of the Company.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: In Maharashtra prior to 2017, Octroi charge was levied for inward material but from 01.01.2017 Octroi was abolished and Local Body Tax (LBT) was levied. In Taloja Copper Project (TCP) of Hindustan Copper Ltd. (HCL), LBT charge was levied on the value of Cathode received at TCP from 01.01.2017 to 31.03.2017 and 01.04.2017 to 30.06.2017. The demand is of approx. Rs.58 crore. Status as per Last Disclosure: The matter has still not been heard and next hearing date is awaited.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Malanjkhand Copper Project (MCP), a unit of Hindustan Copper Limited filed an appeal on 12.05.2009 vide Case No. MJC 1 of 2016 before the Civil Court, Baihar challenging notice dated 18.01.2007 received from the Municipal Council, Malanjkhand demanding a sum of Rs.74.87 crore against Terminal Tax with 10 times penalty for the period 2000-2006. Vide final judgment dated 28.07.2025, the Civil Court, Baihar rejected HCL/MCP’s appeal. On 07.05.2025, HCL filed an Application before AS & FA, Ministry of Mines for amicable resolution of the matter under AMRCD. The matter is pending under AMRCD for Amicable Resolution. On 16.10.2025, HCL has filed a Revision Application before the Court of Additional District Judge, Baihar, praying for setting aside the Demand Bill dated 03.01.2007 issued by the Municipal Council, Malanjkhand. The Civil Court, Baihar vide its judgment and order dated 28/07/2025 passed in MJC No.01/2016 rejected HCL’s appeal. Hence, the present revision petition is filed by HCL/MCP. Status as per Last Disclosure: The matter is pending under AMRCD for Amicable Resolution.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Revision Application before the Court of Additional District Judge, Baihar for Case. No. MJC 1 of 2016, Civil Court, Baihar Hindustan Copper Limited, Malanjkhand Copper Project Vs. Municipal Council, Malanjkhand
tax_litigation.status: The revision petition is filed before the Civil Court, Baihar and the matter is also pending under AMRCD for Amicable Resolution.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Malanjkhand Copper Project (MCP), a unit of Hindustan Copper Limited filed Special Leave Petition No. 14928 of 2014 before the Supreme Court of India challenging notice dated 31.10.2012 received from the Municipal Council, Malajkhand demanding a sum of Rs.188.68 crore against Terminal Tax with 10 times penalty for the period 2006-2012. Vide Order dated 17.02.2025 Special Leave Petition No. 14928 of 2014, the Supreme Court directed HCL to deposit 50% of Rs.188.68 crore within 8 weeks from 17.02.2025. Subsequently, HCL/MCP filed a Modification Application No. 838 of 2025 in respect of Order dated 17.02.2025 passed by the Supreme Court in SLP (C) No. 14928 of 2014, praying for allowing HCL to deposit Rs. 5.3 crores, which is the difference of Terminal Tax calculated by the Municipal Council, i.e., Rs. 17,18,94,364/- and amount paid by HCL/MCP as per self-assessment, i.e., Rs. 11.88 crores. Vide Order dated 05.05.2025, the Supreme Court dismissed HCL/MCP's application On 14.05.2025, HCL filed an application before the AS & FA, Ministry of Mines, Government of India under the Administrative Mechanism for Resolution of CPSE's Disputes (AMRCD) mechanism to get relief. On 05.08.2025, Municipal Council Malanjkhand filed Contempt Petition (Civil) No. 628 of 2025 against Shri Nagesh Shenoy, ED & Unit Head, HCL/MCP for contempt of Order of the Hon’ble Supreme Court dated 17.02.2025 in SLP (C) No. 14928 of 2014. HCL has filed reply in the matter on 07.10.2025. Status as per Last Disclosure: The matters are pending before the Courts.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Contempt Petition (Civil) No. 628 of 2025, Supreme Court Municipal Council , Malanjkhand Vs. Nagesh Shenoy
tax_litigation.status: The last date of hearing was 24.09.2026, and the next date of hearing is 04.01.2027.

operating_notes.text: Total mine expansion capex estimated at ₹7,188.60 Cr between 2026 and 2030.
ICRA reaffirmed [ICRA]AA+ (Stable) and [ICRA]A1+ ratings across ₹2,100 Cr bank facilities and ₹100 Cr commercial paper on April 29, 2026.
HCL and MOU partner teams visited exploration sites in Chile from 20th to 30th April 2026 for site study of copper blocks.
Gujarat Copper Plant operations to be restarted via a 20-year revenue sharing model with Lohum Materials Pvt. Ltd.
Q1FY27 consolidated revenue of ₹936.5 Cr was 19% below Q4FY26's ₹1,156.08 Cr, the highest quarter in memory.
Changes in inventories were a ₹37.21 Cr credit in Q1FY27, continuing the drawdown seen in Q1FY26 (-₹30.72 Cr).
The company operates as a single segment (copper ore mining and processing through continuous copper wire rods) under Ind AS 108.
FY27 ore production target raised to 5.90 MTPA, up 26% YoY from 4.71 MTPA
5-year roadmap targets 12.20 MTPA ore production by FY29-30
Malanjkhand expansion to 5.00 MTPA, Khetri concentrator to 3.00 MTPA
BSE and NSE each fined ₹14,43,140 (₹12,23,000 plus 18% GST) for the June 2026 quarter over board composition and audit, NRC, stakeholder and risk committee constitution.
Hind Copper plans ₹7,000 Cr capex over 5-6 years for mine expansion
Hind Copper targets 12.20 MTPA ore production by FY29-30
Hind Copper to expand Malanjkhand to 5.00 MTPA and Khetri to 3.00 MTPA by FY30
Jabalpur Commercial Court stayed an arbitration award against HCL on condition of a 50% bank guarantee and a 50% asset-valuation bond; Section 34 challenge to be heard after deposit.
ICRA upgraded HCL's long-term rating to [ICRA]AAA (Stable) from [ICRA]AA+ (Stable) and reaffirmed short-term [ICRA]A1+ on ₹2,200 Cr total facilities (₹2,100 Cr bank facilities + ₹100 Cr CP).

timeline.summary: Hindustan Copper unveiled Vision 2030 roadmap detailing ₹7,188.60 Cr mine expansion capex to raise ore capacity to 12.20 MTPA by FY30.
ICRA reaffirmed ratings on ₹2,100 Cr bank facilities at [ICRA]AA+ (Stable)/[ICRA]A1+ and ₹100 Cr commercial paper at [ICRA]A1+.
Hindustan Copper disclosed details of pending litigations and disputes with potential financial implications of ₹2,026 Cr.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹1,156.08 Cr (+58.1% YoY), net profit ₹444.27 Cr (+137.4% YoY).
Executed NDA with CODELCO, engaged transaction advisor, and completed Chilean copper exploration site visits.
On behalf of the President of India, Vivek Kumar Sharma (AT/Director, Ministry of Mines) declared no encumbrance on Hindustan Copper Ltd shares for FY2026 under SEBI’s Regulation 31(4).
BSE and NSE imposed fines of ₹9.56 lakh each on Hindustan Copper for non-compliance with board and committee composition regulations for the quarter ended March 2026.
Hindustan Copper disclosed that the Jharkhand Water Resource Department reassessed its water consumption demand down to ₹87.93 crore.
Hindustan Copper approved awarding a 20-year revenue-sharing contract to Lohum Materials to restart the Gujarat Copper Plant.

Hindustan Copper reported Q1FY27 consolidated revenue of ₹936.5 Cr (up 81.4% YoY) and PAT of ₹352.37 Cr (up 162.5% YoY) with EBITDA margin of 54.19%, while the auditor flagged the absence of independent directors since November 2024.
2026-08-14: Ministry of Mines appoints Ashish Kumar Khetan and Madhumita Daolagupu as independent directors
2026-08-18: Hind Copper raises FY27 ore production target to 5.90 MTPA and outlines 5-year roadmap to 12.20 MTPA
Promoter (President of India) announced an offer for sale of up to 2.90 Cr shares (3.00% of capital) at a floor price of ₹514 per share, to be conducted on August 25-26, 2026.

2026-08-26: BSE and NSE fined Hindustan Copper ₹14,43,140 each for June 2026 quarter non-compliance with board composition and committee constitution rules; company blames pending Ministry of Mines director appointments.
FY26 annual report filed with unmodified audit opinion and emphasis on provisional revenue recognition, pending legal matters, and contingent liabilities of ₹1,262.34 Cr
Hind Copper outlined a ₹7,000 Cr capex plan to expand mining capacity from ~4 MTPA to 12.20 MTPA by FY29-30.

2026-09-22: Commercial Court, Jabalpur granted HCL a conditional stay on an arbitration award won by the IVRCL-MCCDL-TCL-DM Consortium, requiring a 50% bank guarantee and a 50% asset-backed bond before hearing HCL's Section 34 challenge.
ICRA upgraded Hindustan Copper's long-term rating to [ICRA]AAA (Stable) from [ICRA]AA+ (Stable) and reaffirmed short-term [ICRA]A1+ on ₹2,200 Cr of bank facilities and commercial paper.
Hindustan Copper Ltd’s shareholders at the 59th AGM on 23.09.2026 approved dividend of ₹1.86 per share (₹5 face value) for FY 2025-26, payable on 16.10.2026.
Hindustan Copper reported FY26 revenue of ₹3,078 Cr (up 49% YoY) and PAT of ₹921 Cr (up 97% YoY) at its 59th AGM on 23.09.2026.

Hindustan Copper Ltd’s 59th AGM (23.09.2026) passed dividend declaration (99.34% approval) and re-appointed **Sanjeev Kumar Sinha** (91.05%) and **RVN Vishweshwar** (91.84%) as directors via remote e-voting.
Hindustan Copper re-designated three senior managers effective on or before 09.10.2026 per office order dated 25.09.2026.
Hindustan Copper informed the exchange that the IVRCL consortium filed an appeal in the MP High Court against the Jabalpur Commercial Court's stay order.
